Rashi on Nedarim 5b:1:1.hebrew: לימא סבר שמואל ידים שאין מוכיחות כו' - דהכא, הואיל ולא אמר ממש "שאני אוכל לך", אמרינן: לא מוכחא מילתא דבאכילה קאמר, ולא מיתסר באכילה:
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:1:1.english: Shall we say Shmuel holds [that] ambiguous intimations, etc. - For here, since he did not actually say "that which I eat of yours," we say [that] the matter is not evident that he was speaking of eating, and he is not forbidden from eating.

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:2:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר ודין די יהוי ליכי וכו' - דקסבר, אי לא כתב ביה ממש ״ודין״, לאו מוכחא מילתא דבהאי גיטא מגרש לה, דידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים:
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:2:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: “And this shall be to you,” etc. - For he holds that if he did not write specifically “and this” in it, it is not evident that he is divorcing her with this bill of divorce, as ambiguous intimations are not intimations.

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:3:1.hebrew: לוקמה למתני' כרבנן - לימא: אע"ג דקאמר "מודר אני ממך" או "מרוחק אני ממך" לחודיה — אסור באכילה, ואע"ג דלא אמר "שאני אוכל לך", דידים שאין מוכיחות הויין ידים — כרבנן, דאמרי: לא צריך למיכתב בגט אלא "הרי את מותרת לכל אדם":
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:3:1.english: Let him establish the Mishnah in accordance with the Rabbis - Let [Shmuel] say: Even though he said "I am avowed from you" or "I am distanced from you" on its own, he is forbidden to eat [of his food], and even though he did not say "that I eat of yours" — for intimations that are not obvious are [valid] intimations, in accordance with the Rabbis, who say: It is not necessary to write in a bill of divorce [anything] other than "Behold, you are permitted to any person."

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:4:1.english: [It] was difficult for him - For he was unable to establish it according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:4:2.hebrew: ליתני שאני אוכל או שאני טועם - למה לי למימר לך? אלא, להכי קתני לך, דקסבר: ידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים. ואי קתני שאני אוכל בלבד ולא קאמר לך, לא הוה משמע דמודר מחבירו, דבעינן ידים מוכיחות. וכי אמר נמי מודרני, ולא אמר שאני אוכל לך, לא משמע דבאכילה קאמר, אלא דלא מישתעינא בהדך:
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:4:2.english: Let it teach: "That I eat," or "that I taste" - Why is it necessary [for the Mishnah] to say "of yours"? Rather, that is why it teaches "of yours": for he holds [that] intimations that are not obvious are not [valid] intimations. And if it had taught "that I eat" alone, and had not said "of yours," it would not imply that he is vowed [forbidden] from his fellow, for we require obvious intimations. And if he also said "I am vowed," and did not say "that I eat of yours," it would not imply that he was speaking of eating, but rather: "that I will not speak with you."

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:5:1.hebrew: מקיש ידות נזירות - כדאמרינן לעיל, דמלהזיר נפקא ידות נזירות:
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:5:1.english: [The verse] juxtaposes intimations of naziriteship - As we said earlier, that intimations of naziriteship are derived from [the word] “lehazir” [to consecrate himself].

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:5:2.hebrew: מה נזירות בהפלאה - דבעינן שיפרש לנזירות, דכתיב: ״כי יפליא״ (במדבר ו), אף ידות נמי בעינן שיפרש לדיבורו; דאי לא מפרש, לא הוי כלום, דידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים:
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:5:2.english: Just as naziriteship is with a distinct articulation - That we require that he specify his intention for naziriteship, as it is written: “When one clearly utters” (Numbers 6); so too with intimations, we also require that he specify his statement, for if he does not specify, it is nothing, since ambiguous intimations are not valid intimations.

Rashi on Nedarim 5b:7:1.hebrew: דבעינן כריתות - שכורת בינו לבינה, דבעינן שיפסיק לדיבורו:
Rashi on Nedarim 5b:7:1.english: As we require severance - That [the document] sever between him and her, for we require that he effect a severance in his statement.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:1:1.hebrew: לימא קסבר שמואל ידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים מדקאמר מודרני ממך שרי - ומשני: "אין", כלומר: ודאי סבר דלא הויין ידים, ומוקי לה למתניתין כרבי יהודה. דתנן: "גופו של גט: 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם'; רבי יהודה אומר: 'ודין דיהוי ליכי מינאי אגרת' וכו'". במאי קמיפלגי? רבנן סברי: ידים שאין מוכיחות הויין ידים, ולא בעי "ודין" וכו'. ורבי יהודה סבר: לא הויין ידים, מדקבעי לומר "ודין", דאי לא כתב "ודין" בגט — הוי כמגרש בדבורא בעלמא, ושטר ראיה בעלמא הוא. וכן משמע פ' המגרש, דקאמר דקריא למוכיחו' "מודין". ולקמן בשמעתין משמע דהמוכיח הוי מלישנא "דמנאי", מדקאמ': "עד כאן לא קאמר התם לא בעי' ידים מוכיחות אלא גבי גט, דאין אדם מגרש אשת חבירו" — אלמא דמלישנא "דמנאי" קדייק:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:1:1.english: Shall we say that Shmuel holds ambiguous intimations are not intimations, since he said: "I am avowed from you" is permitted - And [the Gemara] answers: "Yes," meaning, he certainly holds that they are not [valid] intimations, and he establishes the mishna in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda. As we learned [in a mishna]: "The essence of a bill of divorce is: 'You are hereby permitted to any man.' Rabbi Yehuda says: 'And this shall be to you from me a document...', etc." In what do they disagree? The Rabbis hold: Ambiguous intimations are [valid] intimations, and [the bill of divorce] does not require "and this...", etc. And Rabbi Yehuda holds: They are not [valid] intimations, since he requires [him] to state "and this", for if he did not write "and this" in the bill of divorce, it would be as though he divorced [her] merely by a spoken statement, and [the bill of divorce] is merely a document of evidence. And so it implies in the chapter [entitled] HaMegareish, which says that it designates the clarification [as deriving] from "and this." And later in our sugya it implies that the clarification is from the phrasing "from me" [minai], since it states: "Only there did [they] say we do not require obvious intimations, regarding a bill of divorce, for a person does not divorce his fellow's wife" — which shows that it deduces [this] from the phrasing "from me."

Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:3:1.hebrew: ואמאי דחיק שמואל לאוקמא מתני' כרבי יהודה לוקמא כרבנן - תימה: הלא יש לו לאוקמה כר' יהודה משום דס״ל כוותיה? ויש מתרצים, דמוטב לאוקמא כרבנן, ואע״ג דהוא לא ס״ל. ועתה, להך לישנא משמע דשמואל סבר דידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים; והכי מוכח סוגיא דקידושין (דף ה:) גבי "הרי את מאורסת", דקאמר: "לימא קסבר שמואל ידים שאין מוכיחות הויין ידים? לא, דאמר: הרי את מאורסת לי, אבל אי לא אמר לי — לא", והיינו כסוגיא דהכא. מיהו תימה גדול: מאי פריך "מאי דוחקיה לאוקמה מתני' כר' יהודה"? דשינויא דשנינן שנויא דחיקא הוא, מוטב לאוקמה כרבנן והוא לא ס״ל?! ועוד, הקשה הר״ר יוסף מהאי דפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף כו.), דקאמר: הכותב טופסי גיטין צריך שיניח מקום האיש ומקום האשה ומקום הזמן; וקאמר שמואל עלה דההיא: אף מקום "הרי את מותרת לכל אדם", פי' משום דהוא עיקר של גט. ואי סבירא ליה כר' יהודה, א״כ צריך שיניח מקום "ודין", שהרי "ודין" הוי עיקר לר' יהודה! להכי ל״ג (אין), כ״א: "ושמואל מוקי לה למתני' כר' יהודה", והוא סבר לה כרבנן; ואז ניחא, דפריך שפיר: לוקמא כרבנן, כיון דגם הוא סבר כרבנן. מיהו קשה מההיא דקידושין, דמשמע שמואל אית ליה דלא הויין ידים. ור״י מחלק בידים שאין מוכיחות גרועות כי ההיא דקידושין, דאם לא אמר "לי" הויין גרועות טפי מדאי (דאדם עשוי לקדש אשה לחבירו); וכן ההיא דנזיר, דפריך עלה, דאמר: האומר "אהא", ה״ז נזיר, ופריך: ודילמא "אהא בתענית" קאמר? ומוקי שמואל: שהיה נזיר עובר לפניו. ולהכי צ״ל הכא: "לימא קסבר שמואל ידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים?" ומשני: "לא, שמואל מוקי לה למתני' כר' יהודה" — פירוש: לעולם קסבר הויין ידים חשובות כי הכא, "מודרני ממך", ומוקי לה למתני' כר' יהודה והוא לא סבירא ליה. ובהא ניחא ההיא דריש פ״א דנזיר, משום ד"אהא" הוי ידים גרועות — משמע כוליה גופיה, וזהו תענית, דנזיר לא הוי כוליה גופיה, ולהכי צריך לאוקומה בנזיר עובר לפניו; וכן ההיא דקידושין, כדפי' התם. ור״ת גרס "אין". השתא יש ליישבו, ודייק: "אין", ידים גרועות כי התם לא הויין ידים, אבל ידים חשובות ס״ל דהויין ידים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:3:1.english: "And why does Shmuel strain to establish the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda? Let him establish it in accordance with the Rabbis" - [This is] astounding: Does he not have to establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda because he holds in accordance with him? And some answer that it is preferable to establish [a mishnah] in accordance with the Rabbis, even though he [himself] does not hold in accordance with them. And now, according to this version, it implies that Shmuel holds that ambiguous intimations are not valid intimations. And so proves the sugya in Kiddushin (5b) regarding [the case of]: "Behold, you are betrothed," where it says: "Shall we say that Shmuel holds ambiguous intimations are valid intimations? No, [it is a case] where he said: Behold, you are betrothed to me; but if he did not say 'to me,' no [she is not betrothed]." And this is in accordance with the sugya here. However, it is a great wonder: What is [the Gemara's] question, "What is his strain to establish the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?" For was the resolution that we answered a strained resolution, [such that] it would be better to establish it in accordance with the Rabbis even though he does not hold in accordance with them?! And furthermore, Harav Rabbi Yosef raised a difficulty from that which is stated in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 26a), which states: "One who writes blank forms of bills of divorce must leave blank the space for the man, the space for the woman, and the space for the date"; and Shmuel said regarding that [mishnah]: "Also the space for [the formula]: Behold, you are permitted to any man" — explanation: because it is the essential part of the bill of divorce. And if he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, if so, he should require leaving blank the space for "and this" [vedein], for behold, "and this" is the essential part according to Rabbi Yehuda! For this reason, we do not read "(Yes)" [In], but rather: "And Shmuel establishes the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda," while he holds in accordance with the Rabbis; and then it works out well, for it asks correctly: Let him establish it in accordance with the Rabbis, since he too holds in accordance with the Rabbis. However, there is a difficulty from that [sugya] in Kiddushin, which implies that Shmuel holds that they are not valid intimations. And the Ri distinguishes [between levels of ambiguity] in [cases of] inferior ambiguous intimations, like that [case] in Kiddushin — where if he did not say "to me," they are far more inferior, because a person is prone to betroth a woman on behalf of his fellow; and similarly that [sugya] in Nazir, which objected concerning that which [the mishna] stated: "One who says: Behold, I shall be [eheyeh], he is a nazirite," and it objected: "And perhaps he meant: Behold, I shall be in fasting?" And Shmuel establishes it [as a case] where a nazirite was passing before him; and therefore it must be said here: "Shall we say that Shmuel holds ambiguous intimations are not valid intimations?" And it answers: "No; Shmuel establishes the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda" — explanation: actually, he holds that substantial intimations are valid intimations, like here: "I am avowed from you" [mudrani mimakh], yet he establishes the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda even though he does not hold in accordance with him. And through this, that [matter] at the beginning of the first chapter of Nazir is resolved, because "Behold, I shall be" is an inferior intimation — it implies his entire body, and this is fasting, whereas a nazirite is not his entire body; and therefore it was necessary to establish it [as a case where] a nazirite is passing before him. And similarly that [case] in Kiddushin, as we explained there. And Rabbeinu Tam reads "Yes" [In]. Now it can be resolved, and [the Gemara] infers: "Yes," inferior intimations like there are not valid intimations, but substantial intimations he holds are valid intimations.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:4:1.hebrew: קשיתיה - מאי איריא התם "שאני אוכל לך"? בלא "לך" נמי! אלא ש"מ דלא הויין ידים. וקשה מברייתא דלעיל, דאמר "שאני אוכל לך" — משמע כמו כן דאי לא אמר "לך" לא מועיל? וי"ל: דכיון דגלי ד"מודרני ממך" מועיל, משמע ממילא "לך" לאו דווקא, ובלא "לך" נמי מהני:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:4:1.english: [The Mishnah] was difficult for him - Why specifically there [did it teach]: "That which I eat of yours"? Even without "of yours" [it should take effect] as well! Rather, conclude from this that [ambiguous intimations] are not [valid] intimations. And [this] is difficult from the baraita above, for it states "that which I eat of yours," which implies likewise that if one did not say "of yours," it is not effective! And it can be answered that since [the baraita] revealed that "I am avowed from you" is effective, it implies automatically that "of yours" was not meant precisely, and even without "of yours" it is also effective.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:4:2.hebrew: ליתני שאני אוכל (לך) שאני טועם - פי': בלא "לך". וא"ת: א"כ, לא הוה ידעינן למאן קאמר? וי"ל: דמיירי במסרבין בו לאכול והוא ממאן, וא"כ לאותו שמפציר בו לאכול קאמר: "שאני טועם", "שאני אוכל" משלך, ואפי' בלא "לך" שמעינן הכי. וא"ת: אכתי מאי תירץ דהנך ברייתא דלעיל דקתני "אסור" תרי זמני, דמשמע ד"מודרני" לחוד אסור ולא "שאני אוכל לך"? וי"ל: כיון דאוקמא טעמא דשמואל משום דידים שאין מוכיחות, דפליגי תנאי בעלמא בגיטין, א"כ נתרץ דהנך ברייתא דלעיל כרבנן דרבי יהודה, דסברי דידים שאין מוכיחות הויין ידים, ושמואל סבר כר' יהודה. דמעיקרא, שלא היה מעמיד טעמא דשמואל משום שאין מוכיחות, וא"כ הוי טעמא דשמואל משום דלא חשוב יד "מודרני" בלא "שאני אוכל", להכי הוה קשיא ליה לשמואל מהנך ברייתא, דלא מוכיחות פלוגתא דתנאי בהכי; אבל השתא דטעמא דשמואל משום שאין מוכיחות, ניחא, כדפרי'. צ"ע לשמואל: כ"שאני אוכל" בלא "מודרני", אם מועיל אם לאו? ופר"י: כר' יהודה דמתני', שאומר "שאני אוכל לך", משמע ד"שאני אוכל לך" מועיל בלא "מודרני", אפי' לשמואל. וכ"נ, דודאי "מודרני" בלא "שאני אוכל לך" הוי ידים שאין מוכיחות, כדמפרש טעמא: דילמא "דלא משתעינא בהדך" קאמר; אבל כ"שאני אוכל לך" או "איני טועם לך" הוו ידים מוכיחות. והקשה ריצב"א: א"כ, לא מצינו ידים ורגלים! דא"כ, כל מה שידבר אדם עם חבירו יהא נדר; שאם אמר: "אני אוכל" או "אוכל לך" הוי נדר, לגי' ד"שאני אוכל"! וי"ל: דלא קשה מידי, דווקא כ"שאני אוכל" או ב"שאיני" בשי"ן הוי יד, לפי [שחטף] וחסר [ומנע] לשונו, שמדלג "קונם" שהיה לו לומר או בתחילה או בסוף; אבל "אני אוכל לך" או "איני אוכל לך" בלא שי"ן לא הוי יד כלל. וא"ת: כיון ד"שאני אוכל לך" מועיל בלא "מודרני", אבל "מודרני" אינו מועיל בלא "שאני אוכל לך", מנלן ד"שאני אוכל" הוי יד לנדר? דילמא הוי יד לשבועה, שמדלג "שבועה" לכתחילה? וי"ל: דבשבועה רגילות לומר: "שבועה שאוכל" או "שלא אוכל", אבל "שאני" או "שאיני" שייך לנדרים. וא"ת: למאי דפרישית ד"שאני אוכל" הוי יד בלא "מודרני" גם לשמואל, והא לעיל בתחילת סוגיא, כדפריך ליה מהנך ברייתא, משני שמואל: "דברייתא שניה, וכבר אמר מודרני ממך" — משמע בהדיא ד"שאני אוכל" לא מהני בלא "מודרני"! ויש לדחות: שלא בא אלא להשמיענו ד"מודרני" אינו מועיל בלא "שאני אוכל לך". ועי"ל: דודאי מעיקרא, שהיה סובר טעמא דשמואל דלא הוי "מודרני" יד כלל בלא "שאני אוכל לך", אז ודאי צריך לומר דה"ה "שאני אוכל לך" לא הוי יד ואינו מועיל בלא "מודרני"; אבל למסקנא דאסיקנא דטעמא דשמואל משום יד, נאמר ודאי ד"שאני אוכל" הוי מוכיח שפיר בלא "מודרני", כדפרישית. א"כ, גם לשמואל מועיל "שאני אוכל" בלא "מודרני". כ"נ למהר"ף נ"ע. מיהו ר"י פירש, ד"שאני אוכל" אינו מוכיח בלא "מודרני":
Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:4:2.english: "Let it teach: That I eat, (of yours,) that I taste" - Explanation: Without "of yours." And if you say: If so, we would not know to whom he is speaking [whose food he is forbidding]! And one can say: It is dealing with [a case where] they are pressing him to eat and he refuses, and if so, it is to that person who is urging him to eat that he is saying: "[That] I taste," "[That] I eat" from yours, and even without "of yours," this is understood. And if you say: Still, how did he resolve those baraitot above [5a] that taught "he is forbidden" twice, which implies that "I am vowed" by itself is forbidden, and not [only in conjunction with] "that I eat of yours"? And one can say: Since Shmuel's reason was established as being because of intimations that are not obvious [yadot she'ein mochichot], regarding which Tannaim disagree elsewhere in Gittin, if so, we can resolve those baraitot above according to the Rabbis who dispute Rabbi Yehuda, who hold that intimations that are not obvious are [valid] intimations, whereas Shmuel holds according to Rabbi Yehuda. For initially, when [the Gemara] had not yet established Shmuel's reason as being because they are not obvious — and if so, Shmuel's reason was that "I am vowed" without "that I eat" is not considered an intimation at all — therefore it was difficult for Shmuel from those baraitot, as they did not demonstrate a dispute between Tannaim regarding this. But now that Shmuel's reason is because they are not obvious, it is settled, as we explained. It requires examination according to Shmuel: In [the case of] "that I eat" without "I am vowed," whether it is effective or not. And Ri explained: According to Rabbi Yehuda of our Mishnah, where one says "that I eat of yours," it implies that "that I eat of yours" is effective without "I am vowed," even according to Shmuel. And so it appears, for certainly "I am vowed" without "that I eat of yours" is an intimation that is not obvious, as [the Gemara] explains the reason: "Perhaps he is saying: '[I am vowed from you] that I will not speak with you'"; but [when one says] "that I eat of yours" or "that I do not taste of yours," these are obvious intimations. And Ritzba raised a difficulty: If so, we cannot find our bearings! For if so, anything a person says to his fellow would become a vow! For if he said "I will eat" or "I will eat of yours," it would be a vow, according to the reading of "that I eat" [which omits the word "vowed"]! And one can say: It is not difficult at all. Specifically [saying] "that I eat" [she'ani okhel] or "that I do not [eat]" [she'eini] with a shin is an intimation, because he curtailed, truncated, and held back his speech, in that he skipped [the word] konam that he should have said either at the beginning or at the end; but "I will eat of yours" [ani okhel lakh] or "I will not eat of yours" [eini okhel lakh] without a shin is not an intimation at all. And if you say: Since "that I eat of yours" is effective without "I am vowed," whereas "I am vowed" is not effective without "that I eat of yours," from where do we know that "that I eat" is an intimation for a vow? Perhaps it is an intimation for an oath, where he skipped [the word] "oath" at the outset [intending an oath that I eat]? And one can say: In the case of an oath, the common practice is to say: "An oath that I will eat [she'okhal]" or "that I will not eat [shelo okhal]"; but "that I [she'ani]" or "that I am not [she'eini]" pertains to vows. And if you say: According to what I explained, that "that I eat" is an intimation without "I am vowed" even according to Shmuel — but above at the beginning of the sugya [5a], when [the Gemara] challenged him from those baraitot, Shmuel answered: "The second baraita [deals with a case where] he had already said: 'I am vowed from you'" — which implies explicitly that "that I eat" is not effective without "I am vowed"! And one can reject [this proof]: It only came to teach us that "I am vowed" is not effective without "that I eat of yours." And furthermore one can say: Certainly initially, when [the Gemara] thought Shmuel's reason was that "I am vowed" is not an intimation at all without "that I eat of yours," then certainly one had to say that the same applies to "that I eat of yours": it is not an intimation and is not effective without "I am vowed." But in the conclusion, where we concluded that Shmuel's reason is because of an intimation [that is not obvious], we say: Certainly "that I eat" indicates [the vow] well without "I am vowed," as I explained. If so, even according to Shmuel, "that I eat" is effective without "I am vowed." So it seemed to Maharaf, may he rest in Eden. However, Ri explained that "that I eat" is not [sufficiently] obvious without "I am vowed":

Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:5:1.hebrew: אמר קרא נזיר להזיר - לרבות ידות נזירות כנזירות: מה נזירות בהפלאה, אף ידות נזירות בהפלאה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:5:1.english: “The verse states: ‘A nazirite, to consecrate himself’” - [This serves] to include intimations of naziriteship as [equivalent to] naziriteship: Just as naziriteship [must be expressed] with distinct articulation, so too, intimations of naziriteship [must be expressed] with distinct articulation.

Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:8:1.hebrew: ע"כ לא קאמרי רבנן דלא בעינן ידים מוכיחות אלא גבי גט משום דמוכח דמיניה הוא דאין אדם מגרש אשת חבירו אבל בעלמא מי שמעת להו - תימה לר"י: תיקשי ליה ברייתא דלעיל, "מודרני ממך אסור", אלמא דהויין ידים! וקשה לאביי מתני', דאמר: "שאני אוכל לך", אבל בלא "לך" — מותר! וי"ל, דלא ס"ל לאביי כשמואל; אבל י"ל ד"לך" לאו דוקא; או שמא למסקנא ניחא, דאביי כרבנן ורבא כרבי יהודה. אבל קשה, דבפ"ב דנזיר (דף סב.) קאמר איפכא, דאביי אית ליה הויין ידים! וי"ל, דהני שיטות הפוכות שבתלמוד, וההיא דהתם כאיכא דאמרי; אבל גירסא דהכא כר' יהודה, כדמוכח התם [עיין תוס' נזיר שם ד"ה איש]:
Tosafot on Nedarim 5b:8:1.english: "The Rabbis say that we do not require obvious intimations only with regard to a bill of divorce, because it is obvious that it is from him, as a man does not divorce the wife of his fellow; but generally, did you hear them?" - It is astonishing to the Ri: Let the baraita above pose a difficulty to him [Rava]: "[If one says:] 'I am vowed from you' — he is forbidden," which shows that they are [valid] intimations! And our Mishnah poses a difficulty to Abaye, which stated: "[Konam] that I eat to you" — [implying that] but without "to you," he is permitted! And one can say that Abaye does not hold in accordance with Shmuel; alternatively, one can say that "to you" is not meant strictly; or perhaps in the final conclusion [of the Gemara] it is settled, [namely] that Abaye is in accordance with the Rabbis and Rava is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. However, this is difficult, for in the last chapter of Nazir (62a), it says the reverse, that Abaye holds that they are [valid] intimations! And one can say that these are reversed sugyot in the Talmud, and that [version] there is like an alternative version [ika de'amrei]; but the version here [aligning Rava] with Rabbi Yehuda is [the primary one], as is proven there. [See Tosafot in Nazir ibid., s.v. Ish].
